title: Idempotent claim aggregation for multi-tenant proxying
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: In our multi-tenant proxy path we sometimes receive the same logical output frames multiple times (client retry, network duplicate, proxy fan-in). Current ledgering logic attributes each arrival as a separate credit which causes double-charges, skewed rate-limiter state, and spurious quota exhaustion for tenants. This ticket designs and implements an idempotent aggregation layer in the metering pipeline that dedupes merged claims, preserves a provable provenance chain, and reconciles provisional credits against finalized checkpoints. We must handle out-of-order arrivals, midstream model/variant handoffs, attachments and embedded binary payloads, and large fan-in scenarios without degrading p99 metering latency. The solution must integrate with existing ledger anchors and support retroactive backfill when partial finalization occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate logical outputs (same session_id + output_fingerprint) are de-duped within the pipeline and only a single token credit is committed to the tenant ledger
Rate limiter counters reflect deduped counts within 5 seconds for typical streams (<=100ms per-frame processing added overhead)
Provisional credits are created for in-flight fragments and automatically reconciled with final checkpoints; in case of mismatch a compensating reverse entry is emitted and visible in audit logs
System handles 5x burst fan-in without increasing token-error rate or exceeding existing p99 metering latency SLO by more than 10% in benchmark harness
End-to-end e2e tests that inject reordered, duplicated, and partial fragments pass deterministically and validate ledger parity against ground truth harness
tasks: Add deterministic output fingerprinting: canonicalize text + normalized tokenizer length + attachment hash
Introduce claim-aggregator service in metering ingest that maintains short-lived dedupe window keyed by (tenant, session, fingerprint)
Persist aggregator anchors to existing ledger stream with idempotency tokens to make commits retry-safe
Add reconciliation worker that watches provisional vs finalized checkpoint and emits compensating entries for mismatches
Instrument tracing and metrics: dedupe_hits, dedupe_misses, provisional_commit_latency, retrospective_compensations
Write unit tests for fingerprinting and aggregator state machine; write integration tests for reordered/duplicated fragments
Benchmark under synthetic fan-in load and tune memory TTLs for aggregator state
Create rollout plan with 10/30/100% canary and kill-switch to revert to legacy path
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Martinez: Filed after customer incident where a tenant reported 3x token usage during a CDN retry storm. Linked incident: INC-2026-145 (drive doc: https://drive.redwood.example.com/incident/INC-2026-145)

2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Spike completed for fingerprinting approach. Prototype uses normalized unicode NFKC, strip-control-chars, collapse whitespace, then compute tokenizer length + SHA256 of normalized bytes. Initial collisions negligible in harness (0/100k).

2026-03-12 Lena Wu (SRE): Suggested keeping aggregator state in Redis with stream-anchored keys and TTL aligned to session keepalive. Concern: Redis memory under 5x fan-in. Propose bounded LRU and fallback to best-effort ledger commit with specific audit flag.
2026-03-13 Arjun Patel: Implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5891 — includes aggregator, new metrics, and feature flag meter.dedupe_enabled

2026-03-14 Design review note (Monica Ruiz): Ensure the reconciliation worker writes compensating entries with metadata links to the original provisional claim and PR for human auditability (console drill-down). Also request schema change for audit log to include fingerprint and origin_path

2026-03-14 QA lead (Daniel Green): Added e2e harness plan and failing scenario where model-handoff generates different fingerprints for semantically identical outputs due to tokenization differences between model variants. Need deterministic tokenizer versioning in fingerprint to avoid false-negatives.
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint normalization and hashing to guarantee stable outputs across language variants
Integration tests simulating duplicated frames, reordered fragments, partial finalization and midstream model downgrade
Load test: 5k concurrent sessions with synthetic 3x fan-in bursts to validate memory limits and latency impact
Chaos test: kill aggregator worker mid-commit to validate compensating entries are emitted on restart
Manual verification: spot-check tenant ledger entries and console audit traces for sample sessions
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout: meter.dedupe_enabled turned off by default
Canary stage 1: enable for internal tenants (10%) and monitor dedupe_hits, compensations, and p99 metering latency for 48 hours
Canary stage 2: expand to 30% of traffic with stricter monitoring of Redis memory and backfill rates
Full rollout: 100% if no regressions after 72 hours at 30%
Rollback: instant toggle off will route to legacy path; reconciliation worker will run retrospective backfill for canary window
